title: The keepers of what DCLab records: one inventory per run, every file of every workspace kept once under one kind, tables and secrets counted only
request: Keepers for sessions, actions, decisions, conversations, model requests, the audit, test runs and live tests, kept once with their hashes, a workspace without consent keeping counts only.
plan: Classify every file once, in its deepest workspace, first matching class wins, the rest as other.
Logs kept by their new tails, the rest whole when changed.

decisions.decision: One inventory per run instead of a pattern per keeper.
decisions.why: Patterns per keeper missed deep workspaces and kept some files twice; one classification makes 'exactly once' true by construction.

decisions.decision: A kind 'other' for anything no class names.
decisions.why: Collect first, find the use after: nothing is left out.

decisions.decision: Tables anywhere, secrets by name, and cell-quoting keys never kept as content.
decisions.why: The store is pushed to a repository; a row never enters it without a person's yes.

change: dclab_rnd.store.keepers.standard (CLASSES, inventory, scrub, notebook outputs removed), keepers.workspaces (discover, of, base_of), keepers.database (every PostgreSQL table per workspace), Store.keep_log (tails cut at a line break), the index cache.

findings.defect: About 7,100 files in deep workspaces were kept by no keeper.
findings.scenario: Live tests' journeys at depth five and six.
findings.cause: Discovery stopped at depth four and the live-test keeper skipped workspace folders by name.
findings.fix: No depth limit; each file belongs to its deepest workspace.

findings.defect: Some files were kept twice or under the wrong kind.
findings.scenario: A nested workspace's jobs.json as a test and as a task; twin lanes as conversations.
Consent off: the audit counted, a live test's log kept whole.
findings.fix: Every file has its own workspace's consent.

findings.defect: Column previews were kept and pushed.
findings.scenario: 841 drafts and 715 projects carried cell previews.
findings.cause: The store did not scrub as the tester share does.
findings.fix: The cell-quoting keys removed from those files; notebooks without outputs; tables anywhere counted only.

findings.defect: Tables outside data folders were going to be kept.
findings.scenario: person/table.csv in the journeys, found by a dry inventory.
findings.cause: Only data folders were treated as tables.

findings.defect: Two runs at once could keep an older reading after a newer one, and a tail could start mid-line.
findings.scenario: The worker's run and a removal's run on a growing log.
findings.cause: The source was read outside the lock and tails were not cut.
findings.fix: Read under the lock; whole lines only.

findings.defect: Keeping slowed down as the index grew.
findings.scenario: 37 ms per unchanged file at 1,500 entries.
findings.cause: The whole index was parsed twice per keep.
findings.fix: An index cache read incrementally; mended only when torn.

findings.cause: Each file checked against every workspace.
findings.fix: Each file walks up its parents to its workspace.

measurements.name: a dry inventory of the development workspaces
measurements.gate: every file assigned once, nothing left out
measurements.result: 15,024 files over 800 workspaces in 4.8 s, none twice, 3,673 tables counted only, 506 MB as content
limits: One machine's workspaces; a tester's will differ.

outcome: Every file of every workspace is kept exactly once under one kind, its tables and secrets counted, its cell values scrubbed, with PostgreSQL workspaces exported too.
lessons: Measure the inventory on the real folder before trusting a test tree.
Make 'exactly once' structural, not a test of patterns.
risks: The first push of half a gigabyte to the records repository is untested.
